title: variantly — 13 more concepts (h–t), Winter 26-27 re-roll
brief: Owner pins: (1) the Winter 2026-27 trend forecast (10 trends; palette oxblood, burnt sienna, warm ivory, muted teal, glacial blue, charcoal; key line 'human-made texture meets digital surrealism'), (2) the most popular contemporary graphic/web styles a 2025-26 NYU / Parsons / SVA class would study. A pinned brief beats the roll; the dealt challengers were fused and declined against it and their disciplines kept as raises.
question: Which of the 13 new worlds join the switcher?

declined.reason: historical (Warhol Factory); the brief pins contemporary styles
declined.kept: editions of one subject: variation shown as re-renders of the same thing

declined.reason: mid-century ephemera; the brief pins contemporary styles
declined.kept: states stamp themselves and stay visible; provenance and state on the surface
a small fixed ink set per theme

declined.reason: scientific vernacular, not a contemporary design style
declined.kept: every readout is real data; one physical rule governs the page

switcher: Twenty concepts overflow the 7-chip row, so the switcher becomes a two-level picker grouped into four renamed families that fit the Winter 2026-27 set better than the v1 ones: Print & Type: b, d, e, f, o, q, r; Hand & Material: a, k, p, s, t; Screen & Signal: c, h, j; Light & Illusion: g, i, l, m, n. Desktop: a compact trigger (current swatch, letter, name) opens a 4-column popover, one family per column; each tile is a 3-colour chip plus the name set in that concept's display face. Keyboard order stays a to t with roving arrow focus and [ / ] stepping through all 20 without opening the grid. Mobile: bottom sheet with family tabs over a snap-scroll strip of large tiles and 44px prev/next. Persist the choice, deep-link with ?v=<id>, and include a 'shuffle' tile.

options.label: Dither Machine
options.origin: reworked from v1 h Pixel Metropolis (kept the integer-grid discipline, dropped the eBoy city costume)
options.lineage: 1-bit / bitmap revival: Bayer and Atkinson dithering as a contemporary image language (Obra Dinn, Low-Tech Magazine's solar site, Playdate)
options.thesis: Every variant is printed through one 1-bit dither on toothy paper: two inks, a pixel grid, and tone made entirely of pattern, with a digital light sweeping across it.
materials: pre-baked paper tooth tile under the ink
options.typography: Silkscreen for the title (dithered fill) with contemporary Space Grotesk UI; all sizes are integer multiples of the 8px cell
options.background: four pre-baked Bayer threshold tiles stacked as a gradient field; a tonal light sweeps across by stepping background-position in steps(48) over 24s
options.letterLook: dithered voxel: unlit MeshBasic with a 2-tone ordered-dither shader on lit faces, nearest-filtered
options.backdropScene: low-poly landscape rendered through a dither ShaderMaterial (threshold per fragment); orthographic camera orbiting one full turn per 24s
options.motion: stepped and quantised; frames hold, then snap
options.viewport: Title lockup centred over the background composition; switcher and CTA rendered as this world's own objects.
options.risk: Reads as a retro-game filter or Mac Classic nostalgia; 1-bit text below 12px gets illegible; must stay distinct from c Amber Terminal (no green phosphor, no CRT).
sources: Lucas Pope, Return of the Obra Dinn (2018)

raised.raise: Variation is real: every variant swatch is the same image re-dithered with a different threshold, never decorative noise.

options.pairing: paper-tooth print grain + a digital light sweep through the dither

options.label: Liquid Glass
options.lineage: Apple's 2025 Liquid Glass UI (WWDC25): refractive, lensing glass controls floating over content
options.thesis: Variants sit under one sheet of liquid glass that bends and lenses whatever is behind it; choosing is looking through.
materials: refractive glass slabs with specular rims
options.typography: Inter Tight variable for the title, Instrument Sans for UI
options.background: large soft colour fields (radial-gradients) drifting under glass-rim highlights drawn with conic-gradients on a closed 24s path, no backdrop-filter
options.letterLook: glass: MeshPhysicalMaterial transmission 1, thickness 0.6, ior 1.45, light iridescence, thin specular bevel
options.backdropScene: rounded glass capsules merging and separating over a glacial gradient plane, refracting it; 24s cycle
options.motion: fluid, elastic, spring-settled; glass stretches toward the pointer
options.viewport: Title lockup centred over the background composition; switcher and CTA rendered as this world's own objects.
options.risk: Becomes a dated glassmorphism card or an Apple knock-off; text on glass fails contrast fast.
sources: Brand New coverage of the iOS 26 redesign

raised.raise: One physical rule everywhere: everything refracts the same way, controls included.

options.label: Instrument OS
options.origin: reworked from v1 j Night Cockpit (kept honest, state-driven readouts; dropped aviation skeuomorphism)
options.lineage: retro-futurist hardware UI: Teenage Engineering OP-1, Nothing's dot-matrix glyph UI, Braun via Dieter Rams
options.thesis: variantly as a beautiful little device: each variant is a preset on a hardware synth, dialled with knobs and read off a dot-matrix display.
options.typography: Doto (dot-matrix) for the title and readouts, Space Grotesk for UI
options.background: grid of dot-matrix cells (radial-gradient dots) with a level-meter waveform scrolling by background-position over 24s; knob ticks rotate on looped keyframes
options.letterLook: machined: brushed-aluminium MeshStandard bodies with rust and grey rubber inset keys
options.backdropScene: exploded-view hardware unit: knobs, keys and screen parts floating apart and reassembling on a 24s loop
options.motion: tactile and clicky; detents, snaps, short springs
options.viewport: Title lockup centred over the background composition; switcher and CTA rendered as this world's own objects.
options.risk: Product-render cosplay of Teenage Engineering or Nothing; knobs as UI can frustrate on touch.
sources: Teenage Engineering, OP-1 field and TP-7

raised.raise: Every state stamps itself on the device: active preset, loading and kept are visible, nothing disappears.

options.label: Ink & Stitch
options.lineage: tactile imperfection: raw cotton paper, dry-brush ink and visible machine stitching, the handmade-mark revival
options.thesis: Every variant is a swatch-book page of torn ivory paper, brushed ink and rust running stitches, and the stitches lift off the page and hover in 3D.
options.typography: Caveat Brush for the title (brushed), Newsreader for UI
options.background: pre-scanned paper-fibre tile under SVG brushstroke paths revealed by stroke-dashoffset, stitch dashes travelling along seams; 24s loop
options.letterLook: thread-bound: matte paper-white MeshStandard glyphs sewn with rust TubeGeometry stitches piercing the faces
options.backdropScene: a paper sheet with a slow vertex wave whose stitches detach, hover as floating thread loops, then re-sew; 24s
options.motion: hand-paced: strokes draw at uneven speed, stitches pull taut
options.viewport: Title lockup centred over the background composition; switcher and CTA rendered as this world's own objects.
options.risk: Etsy craft-fair cliche; scanned textures look fake if the repeat is visible.
sources: It's Nice That, handmade-mark trend coverage (2025)
Kenya Hara / Nippon Design Center paper work

raised.raise: Imperfection is editioned: each variant gets its own stitch path, never random jitter.

options.pairing: real hand stitching + stitches levitating off the page

options.label: Inflated Chrome
options.origin: new (absorbs the contemporary-list acid / chrome-type style)
options.lineage: inflated and liquid-chrome display type from the acid-graphics and Y2K poster revival
options.thesis: The word is a balloon of liquid chrome: puffy, warped letters reflecting an acid-green wireframe world, with tiny technical captions.
options.typography: Syne ExtraBold for the title (inflated in 3D), Major Mono Display for captions
options.background: perspective wireframe grid (repeating-linear-gradient on a rotateX plane) scrolling toward the viewer, starburst glints rotating; 24s loop
options.letterLook: chrome: MeshStandard metalness 1, roughness 0.05, mirrored environment, inflated (pillowed) extrusions
options.backdropScene: the pillowed chrome wordmark and floating starbursts orbiting over a green wireframe terrain
options.motion: bouncy inflation, glints on a 120bpm grid
options.viewport: Title lockup centred over the background composition; switcher and CTA rendered as this world's own objects.
options.risk: Cheap 2000s screensaver chrome; overlaps g Candy 3D if it goes candy-coloured (it stays mirror-silver only).
sources: Brand New, chrome/inflated type trend notes

raised.raise: Captions carry real data (port, variant count, build ms) like a detector printout.

options.label: Uncanny Mirror
options.lineage: surrealism and reality distortion: Magritte reread through Erik Johansson and Alex Prager, impossible scale and dreamlike light
options.thesis: A cold dream room: a rough plaster wordmark stands on an endless mirror floor, and its reflection shows a different variant than the object.
options.typography: Italiana for the title, Manrope for UI
options.background: horizon split: sky gradient above, mirrored duplicate below with shifted hue; a giant moon disc slides along the horizon on a 24s loop
options.letterLook: plaster cast: rough matte white MeshStandard with hairline cracks; the Reflector copy is recoloured as another variant
options.backdropScene: oversized plaster letters and a tiny doorway on a Reflector floor; the reflection runs a beat out of sync
options.motion: slow and dreamlike; object and reflection slightly out of time
options.viewport: Title lockup centred over the background composition; switcher and CTA rendered as this world's own objects.
options.risk: Surreal stock-art cliche (floating rocks, desert doors); the trick reads as a bug if it isn't clearly intentional.

raised.raise: Break one physical rule only: reflections lie, everything else obeys.

options.pairing: rough plaster object + a lying digital reflection

options.label: Noir Velvet
options.lineage: cinematic drama: film-noir shadow, theatrical spotlight and velvet, as in A24 titles and Saul Bass sequences
options.thesis: variantly as an opening title: one spotlight on oxblood velvet, venetian-blind shadows sweeping across a high-contrast Didone wordmark.
options.typography: Bodoni Moda for the title, Cormorant Garamond small caps for credits
options.background: velvet fold gradients with a radial spotlight pool and diagonal blind-shadow bars sweeping across on a 24s loop; pre-baked film-grain tile
options.letterLook: velvet lacquer: MeshPhysical sheen 1 with oxblood sheenColor and a gold rim bevel
options.backdropScene: a curtain opening on a stage, one shadow-mapped SpotLight casting blind shadows across the title
options.motion: slow, theatrical curtain timing; one dramatic cut per change
options.viewport: Title lockup centred over the background composition; switcher and CTA rendered as this world's own objects.
options.risk: Hollywood cliche, too dark; red-on-black text can fail contrast.

raised.raise: Light is the layout: only the spotlit area holds readable text.

options.label: Swiss Punk
trends: contemporary list: Swiss punk / new grotesk
options.lineage: Swiss punk / new grotesk editorial: Weingart's broken grid reread by Experimental Jetset, Studio Dumbar and Order
options.thesis: A typographic poster that won't sit still: one enormous grotesk word, a visible hard grid, and oxblood rules cutting across it.
options.typography: Archivo (variable width/weight) for the title at poster scale, IBM Plex Mono for captions
options.background: hairline 12-column grid with red bars sliding across columns and giant cropped numerals translating on a 24s loop
options.letterLook: enamel sign: flat matte oxblood and black MeshStandard with crisp chamfers
options.backdropScene: monumental extruded letters rotating as slabs on a grid floor, cropping each other
options.viewport: Title lockup centred over the background composition; switcher and CTA rendered as this world's own objects.
options.risk: A design-student homage poster; the broken grid hurts dense reading. Distinct from e Bauhaus (geometry, primaries) by being type-only.

raised.raise: Grid density courage: show the grid lines, never hide the structure.

options.label: Tenango Thread
options.lineage: neo-folk and cultural craft: Tenango embroidery by Otomí (Hñähñu) artisans of Tenango de Doria, Hidalgo, Mexico
options.thesis: Variants as embroidered panels: flat single-colour animals and flowers in dense satin stitch on white cotton, credited to the craft, with threads that drift as if weightless.
options.typography: Grandstander for the title (stitched outline), Work Sans for UI
options.background: symmetric motif panel from SVG stitch-direction hatching; motifs breathe and a thread line runs round the border, 24s loop
options.letterLook: embroidered: MeshStandard with anisotropic thread normal map, glossy satin
options.backdropScene: an embroidered cloth panel whose birds and deer gently lift off and settle back, loose threads swaying in zero gravity
options.viewport: Title lockup centred over the background composition; switcher and CTA rendered as this world's own objects.
options.risk: Appropriation or generic 'Mexican' decoration; it must credit Tenango de Doria artisans by name, use real motif grammar and avoid pastiche.
sources: Tenango de Doria embroidery cooperatives, Hidalgo
Museo de Arte Popular, Mexico City
Carla Fernández, design with Mexican artisans

raised.raise: Provenance on the surface: a credit line names the craft origin and stays visible.

options.pairing: real satin stitch + threads floating weightless

options.label: Sticker Bomb
options.lineage: digital maximalism: sticker-bombed laptop lids and Gen-Z brand identities, clashing patterns kept readable
options.thesis: Variants arrive as stickers slapped on one device lid: holographic, die-cut, overlapping, yet the wordmark stays clear on a clean white sticker.
materials: vinyl die-cut stickers with white kiss-cut borders
options.typography: Rubik Mono One for the title sticker, Bricolage Grotesque for UI
options.background: dense sticker tiles (CSS shapes and gradients) on brushed aluminium, a few peeling and re-sticking on a 24s loop
options.letterLook: vinyl: glossy MeshPhysical clearcoat, iridescence on holo stickers, white border extrusions
options.backdropScene: a laptop lid where stickers drop in, slap flat with a bounce, and one peels its corner; 24s
options.viewport: Title lockup centred over the background composition; switcher and CTA rendered as this world's own objects.
options.risk: Chaos with no hierarchy. Differs from f Cut & Paste by being glossy digital vinyl on a device, not paper collage.

raised.raise: One clean zone: the title sticker and CTA are never overlapped.

options.label: Kinetic Type
options.lineage: kinetic and variable typography: type as motion, from DIA Studio to variable-font identities
options.thesis: The wordmark is the whole show: 'variantly' stretches, compresses and morphs through its axes, one shape per variant.
materials: flat ink and two signal colours
options.typography: Anybody (variable width 50-150, weight 100-900) for display, Fragment Mono for UI
options.background: rows of the word sliding in alternating directions, font-variation-settings animated through wdth and wght on a 24s loop
options.letterLook: elastic letter: flat MeshStandard with morph targets between condensed and expanded extrusions
options.backdropScene: a ribbon of extruded type wrapped round a rotating cylinder, letters stretching as they pass the front
options.viewport: Title lockup centred over the background composition; switcher and CTA rendered as this world's own objects.
options.risk: A motion-reel gimmick that makes reading impossible; heavy variable animation can jank on low-end devices.

raised.raise: One subject in many editions: the same word reshaped per variant, never new imagery.

options.label: Lived-in Den
options.lineage: warm eclecticism / modern nostalgia: walnut, mixed-era objects and amber lamps, as in record-bar and hospitality interiors
options.thesis: A warm listening room: walnut shelves of objects from different decades, an amber lamp, the variants as records you slide out, and one object quietly floating.
options.typography: Fraunces (soft, wonky axis) for the title, DM Sans for UI
options.background: wood-grain gradient bands with an amber glow pool; record sleeves slide along a shelf by translateX, 24s loop
options.letterLook: walnut: MeshStandard wood map with clearcoat and brass inlay edges
options.backdropScene: a shelf vignette (lamp, records, plant, vintage phone) where one object levitates slightly while the lamp light breathes
options.viewport: Title lockup centred over the background composition; switcher and CTA rendered as this world's own objects.
options.risk: Pinterest mid-century cliche; too cosy for a developer tool.

raised.raise: Mixed eras, one light: everything is lit by the same amber source.

options.pairing: real wood grain + one object hovering against gravity

options.label: Stone & Linen
options.lineage: quiet organic minimalism: natural materials, soft silhouettes and negative space (Aesop, Studio Mumbai, Japandi)
options.thesis: Almost nothing: a linen field, one soft stone silhouette and the word, with a window shadow drifting across as if the sun is moving.
options.typography: Cormorant for the title (light weight), Karla for UI
options.background: linen weave tile with a large soft window-shadow shape moving across the page and one pebble silhouette; 24s loop
options.letterLook: honed stone: rough MeshStandard limestone with soft micro-normals
options.backdropScene: pebbles on a linen plane under a slowly turning light that casts a window shadow; one pebble floats a few millimetres up
options.motion: barely moving; only the light travels
options.viewport: Title lockup centred over the background composition; switcher and CTA rendered as this world's own objects.
options.risk: Reads as empty or an Aesop knock-off; too little for a tool that sells variety.

raised.raise: Negative space is measured: two-thirds of the viewport stays empty around the wordmark.

options.pairing: linen and stone + an impossible floating pebble
